venues.name: Amankora
venues.note: Aman's circuit of five intimate lodges across Bhutan's valleys, you journey lodge to lodge like a pilgrimage, and it remains the country's defining luxury experience.
credentials: MICHELIN Key 2025, Two Keys (Bhutan's top tier)
Aman, the group's flagship Bhutan collection

venues.name: Six Senses Bhutan
venues.note: Five architecturally distinct lodges, the Thimphu hilltop, Paro's 'stone ruins', Punakha's flying farmhouse, bound into one wellness-led circuit.
credentials: MICHELIN Key 2025, One Key
Prix Versailles World Award, Best Hotel Design

venues.name: COMO Uma Paro
venues.note: COMO's serene hillside house over the Paro valley, ten minutes from the airport, and home to Bukhari, the country's best-known table.
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards 2018, among the world's best hotels
COMO Hotels & Resorts

venues.name: andBeyond Punakha River Lodge
venues.note: andBeyond's first owned lodge in Asia, six canvas-and-timber tented suites on the banks of the Mo Chhu, light-footprint safari luxury brought to the Himalaya.
credentials: DestinAsian Luxe List 2024, best new hotels & resorts in Asia

venues.name: Bukhari
venues.note: Named for the Himalayan wood-burning stove at its heart, this circular pavilion at COMO Uma Paro is Bhutan's best-known table, local produce, elegant technique, the valley all around.
credentials: COMO Uma Paro, Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards 2018

venues.name: Babesa Village Restaurant
venues.note: Traditional Bhutanese home cooking in a 500-year-old rammed-earth farmhouse, ema datsi, red rice, the real thing, loved by locals.
credentials: World Culinary Awards 2024, Bhutan's Best Restaurant

venues.name: Paro Taktsang (Tiger's Nest)
venues.note: Bhutan's defining image: a 17th-century monastery clinging to a sheer cliff 900 metres above the Paro valley, reached by a 4-to-5-hour round-trip climb through pine and prayer flags. Guru Rinpoche is said to have flown here on the back of a tigress; the ascent is the emotional centre of any Bhutan trip and doable at a gentle multi-generational pace with horses to the halfway teahouse.
credentials: Bhutan's most iconic pilgrimage and hike

venues.name: Rinpung Dzong (Paro Dzong)
venues.note: The 'Fortress on a Heap of Jewels' rises in whitewashed tiers above the Paro river, a working seat of monks and district administration and the stage for the springtime Paro Tshechu. The covered cantilever bridge below is one of the most photographed sights in the kingdom.
credentials: On Bhutan's UNESCO Tentative List (Bhutanese dzongs)

venues.name: Ta Dzong (National Museum of Bhutan)
venues.note: A round former watchtower above Paro Dzong, now holding over 3,000 works spanning 1,500 years of Bhutanese art, thangkas, bronzes and ritual objects. It gives multi-gen travellers the cultural grounding that makes the rest of the trip legible.
credentials: National museum of Bhutan

venues.name: Kyichu Lhakhang
venues.note: One of the oldest and most sacred temples in Bhutan, said to be among 108 built by a Tibetan king in the 7th century to pin down a demoness across the Himalayas. Small, deeply atmospheric and still living, with two ancient orange trees that fruit year-round in the courtyard.
credentials: Among Bhutan's oldest temples (7th century)

venues.name: Drukgyel Dzong
venues.note: The romantic ruin at the head of the Paro valley, built in 1649 to mark victory over Tibetan invaders and now being carefully reconstructed. On a clear morning the sacred peak of Jomolhari fills the horizon behind it.
credentials: On Bhutan's UNESCO Tentative List (Bhutanese dzongs)

venues.name: Paro town & weekend market
venues.note: A single handsome main street of traditional painted shopfronts, easy to stroll for textiles, thangkas and hand-woven kira. The riverside market brings in valley farmers with red rice, dried chillies, cheese and wild honey.

venues.name: Chele La Pass
venues.note: Bhutan's highest motorable pass at 3,988 metres, an hour's spectacular drive from Paro through spruce and larch to a ridge draped in thousands of prayer flags. On a clear day the sacred Jomolhari and Jichu Drake stand out to the northwest; short walks lead to higher viewpoints.
credentials: Highest motorable pass in Bhutan

venues.name: Kila Nunnery
venues.note: One of Bhutan's oldest nunneries, a cluster of retreat houses tucked into the cliffs just below Chele La and reached on a serene forest walk. The 20-odd nuns keeping it feel a world away from the tourist circuit.
credentials: Among Bhutan's oldest nunneries

venues.name: Traditional farmhouse visit & hot-stone bath
venues.note: Tea, ara and a home-cooked meal inside a rammed-earth Bhutanese farmhouse, followed by the classic dotsho: soaking in river water heated by fire-roasted stones and infused with artemisia. A quiet, deeply local evening that the Aman and COMO lodges also stage beautifully.

venues.name: Archery (datse) demonstration
venues.note: Watch or try Bhutan's national sport, where teams loose arrows at a target a improbable 145 metres away and celebrate each hit with song and dance. Many guides can arrange a friendly local match near Paro.
credentials: Bhutan's national sport

venues.name: Dumtse Lhakhang
venues.note: A rare chorten-shaped temple near Paro, built in 1421 by the iron-bridge saint Thangtong Gyalpo and, by legend, once chained down so it would not fly to heaven. Inside are some of the finest and most complete Buddhist wall paintings in the country.

venues.name: Zuri Dzong hike
venues.note: A gentle 1.5-hour walk to Bhutan's oldest dzong, past a cave where Guru Rinpoche is said to have meditated, ending on a ridge with a full bird's-eye sweep of the Paro valley. The rewarding alternative for those who want a view without the Tiger's Nest climb.

venues.name: Jomolhari base-camp trek (start point)
venues.note: The classic Himalayan trek to the foot of Bhutan's most sacred 7,326-metre peak begins in the upper Paro valley, threading yak pastures and remote hamlets. For the fit traveller it is one of the great multi-day walks of the eastern Himalaya.
credentials: One of Bhutan's classic high-Himalayan treks

venues.name: Buddha Dordenma
venues.note: A 51-metre gilded-bronze Shakyamuni Buddha seated above the capital, housing more than 100,000 smaller Buddhas within. The terrace commands the whole Thimphu valley and is especially moving at first light.
credentials: Among the largest Buddha statues in the world

venues.name: Tashichho Dzong
venues.note: The gleaming white fortress-monastery on the Thimphu river that houses the throne room, government ministries and the central monk body. Its scale and craftsmanship set the standard for Bhutanese architecture, and it glows under floodlight at night.
credentials: Seat of Bhutan's government and central monastic body

venues.name: National Memorial Chorten
venues.note: The most-visited religious landmark in central Thimphu, built in 1974 in memory of the third king. From dawn, elderly locals circle it clockwise turning prayer wheels; it is the most human, living portrait of Bhutanese faith you can witness.

venues.name: Motithang Takin Preserve
venues.note: A forested reserve on the edge of the capital devoted to the takin, Bhutan's improbable national animal, a creature that looks assembled from a goat and a cow. A short, easy, kid-friendly stop with real curiosity value.
credentials: Home to Bhutan's national animal, the takin

venues.name: Folk Heritage Museum
venues.note: A restored three-storey rammed-earth farmhouse that recreates rural Bhutanese life of a century ago, room by room. The most tangible way to understand how most Bhutanese still live outside the towns.

venues.name: Royal Textile Academy & National Textile Museum
venues.note: Bhutan's finest showcase of weaving, where the extraordinarily intricate kira and gho fabrics that clothe the nation are displayed and demonstrated on the loom. Essential for anyone who values craft, and a discreet place to acquire heirloom-grade textiles.

venues.name: Changangkha Lhakhang
venues.note: A 12th-century fortress-temple on a ridge above Thimphu, the oldest in the valley, where local families bring newborns to be named and blessed. The ramparts give a lovely panorama over the capital.
credentials: Oldest temple in the Thimphu valley

venues.name: Thimphu weekend market
venues.note: A riverside pavilion that fills Thursday to Sunday with farmers from across the country: red rice, fiery dried chillies, discs of fresh datshi cheese, ferns, pickles and southern wild honey, plus a handicraft section across the footbridge. The best single window onto everyday Bhutan.

venues.name: The giant prayer wheel at Memorial Chorten & Zilukha
venues.note: Enormous copper-and-gold mani wheels, each packed with millions of printed mantras, that pilgrims turn to release blessings with every rotation. Spinning one in the flow of chanting elders is a small, grounding ritual you will remember.

venues.name: Simply Bhutan living museum
venues.note: A hands-on 'living museum' where you try the national dress, archery, butter-tea and folk song in a recreated village setting. Touristic but genuinely fun and a gentle, engaging option for children and grandparents.

venues.name: Sangaygang viewpoint
venues.note: A short drive to a hillside at 2,685 metres below the telecom tower, giving the classic full-valley view of Thimphu framed in prayer flags. A ten-minute stop that reorients the whole capital for you.

venues.name: Cheri Monastery hike
venues.note: A steep, quiet hour's climb across a covered bridge to the 1620 monastery where Bhutan's unifier established the first monastic body. Deeply peaceful, often shared only with monks and grazing goral on the slopes.
credentials: Site of Bhutan's first monastic community (1620)

venues.name: Tango Monastery hike
venues.note: A 90-minute forest walk to a serene 13th-century Buddhist college north of Thimphu, still a place of retreat and study. Pairs naturally with Cheri for a full, unhurried day in the upper valley away from the crowds.

venues.name: Dochula Pass & the 108 chortens
venues.note: The 3,100-metre pass on the road east from Thimphu, crowned by 108 Druk Wangyal chortens built by the Queen Mother and, on a clear morning, a jaw-dropping line-up of the eastern Himalayan snow peaks. The mountainside cafe here is the classic tea stop en route to Punakha.

venues.name: Punakha Dzong
venues.note: Widely held to be the most beautiful dzong in Bhutan, standing at the confluence of the 'father' and 'mother' rivers and blazing purple with jacaranda in spring. Built in 1638, it was the old capital and remains the winter home of the central monk body; the coronation and royal wedding were held here.
credentials: On Bhutan's UNESCO Tentative List (Bhutanese dzongs)
Often called Bhutan's most beautiful dzong

venues.name: Chimi Lhakhang (the fertility temple)
venues.note: A small 1499 hilltop temple reached on a gentle walk through rice terraces and a village painted with phalluses, dedicated to the irreverent 'Divine Madman' saint Drukpa Kunley. Couples come from across Bhutan and abroad for a fertility blessing; the walk itself is one of the loveliest in the west.

venues.name: Punakha suspension bridge
venues.note: At around 160 metres, one of the longest suspension bridges in Bhutan, swaying gently over the Po Chhu river and hung with prayer flags. A short, exhilarating crossing with dzong and river views, and a fine spot for photographs.

venues.name: Khamsum Yulley Namgyal Chorten walk
venues.note: A beautiful 45-minute walk across the valley floor and up through pine forest to an elaborately painted royal chorten completed in 1999. The rooftop gives the finest panorama over the terraced Punakha valley and its winding rivers.

venues.name: Punakha valley & river
venues.note: At around 1,200 metres, warm, low and green, this is where Bhutan slows down: rice paddies, riverside luxury camps and gentle raft floats on the Mo Chhu past the great dzong. The most relaxed leg of a western Bhutan trip, ideal for multi-gen travellers.

venues.name: Mo Chhu river rafting
venues.note: A gentle scenic float down the Mo Chhu, passing the Punakha Dzong from the water with kingfishers and the occasional heron along the banks. Soft-adventure that suits families and non-paddlers alike.

venues.name: A tshechu festival
venues.note: The great annual masked-dance festivals, held in dzong courtyards, where monks in brocade and carved masks enact the triumph of dharma over chaos before the whole valley in its finest dress. The Paro Tshechu (spring) and Thimphu Tshechu (autumn, the country's largest) are the most spectacular; dates follow the lunar calendar, so plan the trip around them.
credentials: Bhutan's most important religious festivals

venues.name: A monk's blessing
venues.note: A private audience or blessing from a lama in a working temple, the thread of blessed cord tied at the neck and butter lamps lit for one's family. In a country where faith is woven into daily life, it is often the moment travellers remember most.

venues.name: Guided meditation & mindfulness
venues.note: Sunrise meditation in a monastery or lodge shrine room, led by a monk or the resident wellness team at Amankora, Six Senses or COMO. In the last Himalayan Buddhist kingdom this is the natural centrepiece of a slow, restorative trip.

venues.name: Ema datshi & Bhutanese cuisine
venues.note: The national dish is ema datshi, whole chillies stewed in soft cheese, eaten with nutty red rice, and the wider table is unusually kind to vegetarians, with cheese, ferns, buckwheat and mushrooms everywhere. A cooking demonstration or farmhouse lunch turns a meal into an experience.
credentials: Ema datshi is Bhutan's national dish

venues.name: Haa Valley
venues.note: One of Bhutan's least-visited valleys, reached over Chele La, where the pace slows, homestays and farmhouses replace hotels and the twin white-and-black temples of Lhakhang Karpo and Lhakhang Nagpo anchor the valley floor. For travellers who have seen the icons and want the road less travelled.
credentials: Among Bhutan's least-visited valleys

venues.name: Blue poppy & rhododendron season
venues.note: In late spring the high slopes around Chele La and the passes blaze with rhododendron, and the elusive blue poppy, Bhutan's national flower, appears above the treeline. A quiet draw for keen walkers and photographers timing the trip to May and June.
credentials: Blue poppy is Bhutan's national flower

venues.name: Amankora circuit
venues.note: Aman's five intimate lodges in Paro, Thimphu, Punakha, Gangtey and Bumthang let you travel valley to valley without leaving the brand, with private guides, farmhouse dinners and hot-stone baths arranged throughout. The benchmark for a seamless ultra-luxury Bhutan journey.

venues.name: Six Senses Bhutan lodges
venues.note: A parallel five-lodge route across the west, each property designed around a distinct valley theme, with standout spas and dramatic architecture at Thimphu ('flying farmhouse') and Punakha. A strong choice for wellness-led, design-conscious travellers.

venues.name: COMO Uma Paro & Punakha
venues.note: COMO's two hilltop retreats above Paro and in the Punakha valley pair the group's celebrated wellness and cuisine with a warmer, more relaxed feel than the grander houses. Often the best value at the top of the market and excellent for families.

venues.name: Punakha to Gangtey (Phobjikha) extension
venues.note: A day's drive east of Punakha opens the glacial Phobjikha valley, the winter home of the rare black-necked cranes that arrive from Tibet each November and the graceful Gangtey Goenpa monastery above the wetlands. The natural next step for those extending beyond the west.
credentials: Winter roost of the endangered black-necked crane

venues.name: Mojo Park
venues.note: Thimphu's live-music institution since 2011, local and visiting bands, an easy crowd of Bhutanese and expats, and the closest the capital comes to a real night out.
credentials: Genuine standing, Thimphu's best-known live-music venue, on Chang Lam
